metadata.manifest_purpose: Canonical public-safe source for the Lake Como, Blanca, Ellingwood, and Mount Lindsey Companion artifacts.
metadata.manifest_hash_rule: SHA-256 is calculated over the exact bytes of data/trip-manifest.json and is recorded outside this file.

safety_invariants.jurisdiction: Dispatch determines the responding agency from the exact incident location.
safety_invariants.planning: A user-defined planning target is not automatic route authorization.

trip.name: Lake Como / Blanca / Ellingwood / Mount Lindsey 2026
trip.area: Lake Como, Blanca Peak, Ellingwood Point, and Mount Lindsey

planning_times.label: Lake Como approach planned start
planning_times.safety_note: Road clearance, conditions, and driver judgment determine the actual starting point and time.

planning_times.label: Lake Como reach-camp planning target
planning_times.safety_note: This target preserves recovery margin; it does not determine whether travel is permitted.

planning_times.label: Blanca and Ellingwood planned start
planning_times.safety_note: The planned start remains fixed unless the owner creates a new canonical data version.

planning_times.label: Below-exposed-terrain planning target
planning_times.safety_note: This is a user-defined planning target, not a calculated safety cutoff, weather permission, or continuation threshold.

planning_times.label: Mount Lindsey planned start
planning_times.safety_note: Current access, route conditions, and group judgment govern the actual climb.

planning_times.label: Mount Lindsey return/exit planning target
planning_times.safety_note: This is a planning target; access, weather, terrain, pace, and group condition govern reassessment.

camp.name: Lake Como
camp.notes: The frozen source identifies Lake Como camp and a Lake Como area weather point; it does not establish that the point coordinates are the exact campsite.

transportation.usage: Default travel vehicle; actual Lake Como road parking depends on clearance, road condition, weather, and driver judgment.

waypoints.name: Lake Como road start near 8,000 ft
waypoints.route_context: Published lower Lake Como approach start; coordinates are not stored in the frozen source.

waypoints.name: Lake Como road 4WD pull-offs near 8,800 ft
waypoints.route_context: Published higher Lake Como approach start; coordinates and an exact parking location are not stored in the frozen source.

waypoints.name: Lake Como area
waypoints.route_context: Frozen-source weather/reference point for the Lake Como area; not asserted as an exact campsite coordinate.

waypoints.name: Lily Lake Trailhead
waypoints.route_context: Frozen source names the legal Mount Lindsey access trailhead but stores no coordinate or elevation for it.

route_segments.route_name: Lake Como Approach from near 8,000 ft
route_segments.route_notes: Published approach profile. Current route-reference evidence explicitly labels 11.25 miles as round-trip. The 3,900 ft figure is retained as upstream cumulative gain and is not replaced by endpoint subtraction.
route_segments.return_considerations: Road clearance determines the actual starting point; do not force the vehicle higher than conditions support.

route_segments.route_name: Lake Como Approach from near 8,800 ft
route_segments.route_notes: Published approach profile. Current route-reference evidence explicitly labels 8.5 miles as round-trip. The 3,100 ft figure is retained as upstream cumulative gain and is not replaced by endpoint subtraction.
route_segments.return_considerations: Road clearance determines the actual starting point; do not force the vehicle higher than conditions support.

route_segments.route_name: Combo: Blanca + Ellingwood from Lake Como camp
route_segments.route_notes: The connecting ridge has a Class 3 line or a return to the standard trail before reascending; choosing the Class 3 line is a separate decision from choosing the combination.
route_segments.return_considerations: The traverse remains optional. Weather, rock, time, and every climber's comfort decide the sequence.

route_segments.route_notes: Frozen source states that a waiver is required and legal access is from Lily Lake Trailhead via the standard gully or ridge route.
route_segments.return_considerations: The frozen source does not store the trailhead elevation, so no net descent figure is inserted.

decision_points.prompt: Compare the saved forecast timestamp with actual sky, wind, and cloud growth at departure.
At the upper basin, reassess wind, cloud growth, pace, comfort, and group condition.
Before the Blanca–Ellingwood traverse, reassess weather, rock, time, and every climber's comfort; the traverse remains optional.

Turn or descend for thunder or rapidly building convection, balance-impairing wind, worsening altitude symptoms, unacceptable rockfall or route conditions, any climber declining the Class 3 traverse, or exposure after the agreed planning target.
Before leaving service, confirm current Mount Lindsey access and waiver requirements; route conditions and group judgment govern.

emergency_sequence: Provide exact location, mountain, route, elevation, and coordinates if available.
Provide injuries, party size, weather, and current conditions.
Let dispatch determine the responding agency.
communications.draft_behavior: Text and email actions create drafts for review. A draft or copied update is not evidence of delivery; only external transport confirmation establishes delivery.
communications.recipient_handling: No recipient value is canonical. Initial physical values are handwritten outside the repository; any later approved PWA value remains device-local.

external_sources.authority: Trinchera Blanca Ranch access waiver portal
external_sources.title: Mount Lindsey Waiver
external_sources.fact_verified: An executed landowner waiver is required to enter Trinchera Blanca Ranch property for the designated Mount Lindsey summit access route.
external_sources.notes: Scope is hiking access to the summit on the designated route. The portal prohibits route deviation, hunting, camping, overnight use, motorized or wheeled transport, and drones on ranch property; it does not represent the route as maintained or supervised.

external_sources.title: Mount Lindsey
external_sources.fact_verified: CFI documents the recommended Huerfano River Valley route, Lily Lake-area approach, private-land constraints, and rough final road miles.
external_sources.notes: The page says not to park or camp at Singing River Ranch, identifies the posted Huerfano River trailhead, and notes the unmarked cutoff from the Lily Lake trail. It does not publish an exact operational trailhead coordinate or elevation.

external_sources.title: Mount Lindsey Northwest Ridge
external_sources.fact_verified: CMC documents current designated-route access, the required waiver, an 8.5-mile route profile, 3,500 feet of gain, and a 14,055-foot high point.
external_sources.notes: Used for current access and route-profile corroboration. The canonical selected route remains the Northwest Gully, not the ridge variant.

external_sources.title: Summit 2026 — Mt. Lindsey Northwest Gully
external_sources.fact_verified: A current 2026 CMC trip listing treats the Northwest Gully as an active objective and requires the Mount Lindsey access waiver.
external_sources.notes: Corroborates current practical use; it does not supersede the landowner’s restrictions or independently establish a trailhead coordinate.

external_sources.title: Blanca Peak Roadless Area Profile
external_sources.fact_verified: The Forest Service identifies NFSR 580 Upper Huerfano Road as public access to NFST 1308 Lily Lake and limits the described trail to foot and horse travel.
external_sources.notes: Officially verifies the access corridor and trail identity, but the document does not establish an operational parking-point coordinate or elevation.

external_sources.title: National Forest System Trails Feature Layer
external_sources.fact_verified: The official national trail dataset catalog was reviewed as the preferred geospatial source class for NFST 1308.
external_sources.notes: The catalog did not yield a single official parking or trailhead point in this pass; it therefore does not close the Lily Lake operational-location blocker.

external_sources.title: Huerfano/Lily Lake Trailhead
external_sources.fact_verified: The established route reference publishes 37.62361, -105.47278 and 10,700 feet for the Huerfano/Lily Lake trailhead, with rough-road and limited-parking context.
external_sources.notes: Secondary operational evidence only. The coordinate and elevation remain null because no authoritative agency point was established.

external_sources.title: Lily Lake / Huerfano Creek Trailhead
external_sources.fact_verified: A secondary reference publishes approximately 37.623486, -105.472903 and 10,725 feet for a Lily Lake/Huerfano Creek trailhead point.
external_sources.notes: This differs slightly from the 14ers.com point and elevation. Neither value was selected, averaged, or copied into the canonical waypoint.

external_sources.title: Mount Lindsey Northwest Gully
external_sources.fact_verified: The current route page labels the Northwest Gully Easy Class 3 with considerable exposure, 8.25 miles round-trip, and 3,500 feet of gain, and links the required waiver.
external_sources.notes: All four canonical route-profile values agree. Legal access remains limited by the landowner waiver and designated route.

external_sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey and U.S. Board on Geographic Names
external_sources.title: GNIS Domestic Names — Colorado text dataset
external_sources.fact_verified: The July 2026 GNIS extract identifies Lake Como at 37.5695982, -105.5140623; Blanca Peak at 37.5775609, -105.4855987; Ellingwood Point at 37.5824644, -105.4926087; and Mount Lindsey at 37.583803, -105.4446957.
external_sources.notes: Lake Como rounds to the frozen area-reference coordinate. Summit coordinates differ from the frozen route-reference points by small, non-material field distances; the upstream values were retained and not averaged. The current extract does not publish elevations.

external_sources.title: Geographic Names Information System FAQ
external_sources.fact_verified: USGS documents that GNIS summit coordinates represent the highest point, are stored in NAD 83, and that GNIS elevations are approximate rather than official values.
external_sources.notes: Used to interpret coordinate and elevation-method differences; it does not authorize replacing the frozen route-reference points.

external_sources.title: Elevations of Named Summits Over 14,000 Feet Above Sea Level
external_sources.fact_verified: The USGS named-summit table publishes map-era elevations of 14,345 feet for Blanca and 14,042 feet for both Ellingwood and Lindsey.
external_sources.notes: These differ from the frozen modern LiDAR values by 5, 15, and 13 feet. The differences are method-era distinctions and non-material for forecast-reference use; neither representation was silently substituted.

external_sources.title: Blanca Peak
external_sources.fact_verified: The current peak page publishes 37.57753, -105.48569 and a 14,350-foot LiDAR elevation, exactly matching the frozen route/weather reference.
external_sources.notes: Secondary current-method corroboration; the official USGS map/survey representation is separately retained in the evidence record.

external_sources.title: Ellingwood Point
external_sources.fact_verified: The current peak page publishes 37.58257, -105.49248 and a 14,057-foot LiDAR elevation, exactly matching the frozen route/weather reference.
external_sources.notes: Secondary current-method corroboration; the official USGS map-era representation is separately retained in the evidence record.

external_sources.title: Mount Lindsey
external_sources.fact_verified: The current peak page publishes 37.58389, -105.44490 and a 14,055-foot LiDAR elevation, exactly matching the frozen route/weather reference.
external_sources.notes: Secondary current-method corroboration; the official USGS map-era representation is separately retained in the evidence record.

external_sources.title: Lake Como Topo Map
external_sources.fact_verified: The secondary GNIS/topographic representation gives 37.5695982, -105.5140623 and an approximate elevation of 11,749 feet for Lake Como.
external_sources.notes: The coordinate rounds to the frozen area point; the one-foot elevation difference is non-material and was not used to replace the 11,750-foot route-reference value.

external_sources.title: Lake Como Approach
external_sources.fact_verified: The route page explicitly labels 11.25 miles from near 8,000 feet and 8.5 miles from near 8,800 feet as round-trip, with 3,900 feet and 3,100 feet of gain respectively, Class 1, low exposure, and Lake Como near 11,750 feet.
external_sources.notes: This resolves the frozen mileage-scope ambiguity without changing either distance or gain. The page distinguishes lower 2WD access, several 8,800-foot 4WD pull-offs, sparse higher parking, and much harder road above 10,000 feet.

external_sources.title: Lake Como (Blanca Peak) Trailhead
external_sources.fact_verified: The current trailhead page identifies approximately 8,000 feet as the lower trailhead and approximately 8,800 feet as several pull-offs just inside the Forest boundary, with increasing 4WD difficulty above.
external_sources.notes: No vehicle model is certified or authorized. Current, date-specific condition reports were reviewed but not copied into the immutable manifest.

external_sources.title: Blanca and Ellingwood Combination Route
external_sources.fact_verified: The current combination profile gives 7 miles round-trip and 3,000 feet of gain from Lake Como, Class 3, and considerable exposure, and distinguishes the Class 3 ridge from descending to the standard trail before reascending.
external_sources.notes: All canonical profile values agree and the traverse remains optional. No Little Bear objective or unsourced descent was added.

external_sources.fact_verified: NPS separately gives 8,170 feet for the Visitor Center itself.
external_sources.notes: The 30-foot difference reflects the narrower Visitor Center context versus the weather page’s rounded Visitor Center/campground/dunefield context; it is non-material and no value was averaged or replaced.
